findings.passage: SAVE is short for "Safe, Accurate and Verifiable Elections," and requires paper ballots, hand counting, limits absentee ballots, removes early voting, and makes Election Day a state holiday.
findings.note: Her weekly newsletter describes H.4935, which she and other Charleston County members filed. It sets paper ballots, hand counting, fewer absentee ballots, no early voting and a one-day state-holiday election.

findings.passage: These changes are designed to address all of the major concerns, and have been demonstrated to help reduce the chance of any irregularities or outright fraud considerably.
findings.note: She says the H.4935 changes respond to constituent concerns about fraud and invalid voting and would reduce irregularities. The newsletter does not mention voter ID or citizenship.

findings.passage: I proudly voted YES to a constitutional amendment, S.1126, to ensure that only registered citizens can participate in our electoral process.
findings.note: Her Week 17 newsletter (dated Sunday, May 5, 2024) under the heading 'Only Citizens May Vote!' gives her reason for S.1126, the Citizens Only Voting Amendment. It mentions a vote; the vote record itself is linked separately.

findings.passage: Strengthening Families and Communities: The “Help Not Harm” bill protects children from gender transition procedures, and we banned non-citizens from voting through a constitutional referendum.
findings.note: Year-end newsletter (dated Sunday, January 5, 2025) listing what the 2024 session did, naming the citizens-only voting amendment.

findings.passage: This measure makes it clear that only U.S. citizens can vote in South Carolina elections, protecting the integrity of our system as other states like California, Maryland, and Vermont move to allow non-citizens to participate in certain local elections.
findings.note: Weekly newsletter (dated Sunday, April 26, 2026) on S.582, the Citizens-Only Voting Constitutional Amendment, which she says advanced in House Judiciary Committee.

findings.passage: This was already the law, but due to a slightly weaker word, we had to strengthen it to provide absolute clarity.
findings.note: Newsletter page titled May 12th Weekly Update (printed date 'Sunday, May 12, 2026'; May 12, 2026 was a Tuesday, and the text says it was sent after Mother's Day on Monday or Tuesday), on the House passing S.582.

findings.passage: South Carolina is taking action to protect the integrity of our elections and make clear that voting is a right reserved for American citizens only.
findings.note: Same May 12th newsletter, on S.582, the Citizens-Only Voting Constitutional Amendment.
